claim: Elections are held on uniform dates: the first Saturday in May or the first Tuesday after the first Monday in November
quote: the first Saturday in May in an odd-numbered year

claim: County and state officers are elected in November of even-numbered years
quote: The general election for state and county officers shall be held on the first Tuesday after the first Monday in November in even-numbered years.

claim: The general primary is the first Tuesday in March of even-numbered years, with a runoff on the fourth Tuesday in May
quote: The runoff primary election date is the fourth Tuesday in May following the general primary election.

claim: Voting in a party's primary affiliates the voter with that party
quote: A person becomes affiliated with a political party when the person:

claim: City candidates appear on the ballot as independents unless a home-rule charter authorizes partisan nominations
quote: A city charter may authorize nominations of partisan candidates by political organizations for an office of a home-rule city.

claim: School and other district candidates appear on the ballot only as independents
quote: A candidate's name may appear on the ballot only as an independent.

claim: Elections may also fall on the first Saturday in May of an even-numbered year, for any political subdivision other than a county
quote: the first Saturday in May in an even-numbered year, for an election held by a political subdivision other than a county

claim: An election held on a date the uniform-date rules do not allow is void
quote: An election held on a date not permitted by this subchapter is void.

claim: The deadline for most political subdivisions to move their election to the November odd-year date was 31 December 2025
quote: may, not later than December 31, 2025, change the date on which it holds its general election for officers to the November uniform election date in odd-numbered years

claim: A home-rule city can make the date change by resolution, overriding its charter
quote: The change contained in the resolution supersedes a city charter provision that requires a different general election date

claim: Party affiliation from voting in a primary lasts until the end of the voting year
quote: a party affiliation expires at the end of the voting year in which the person became affiliated

claim: A primary voter cannot vote in another party's primary or runoff in the same voting year
quote: A vote in a primary election is void if the voter previously voted in a primary election of another party

claim: Someone who voted in a primary cannot run as an independent for an office that party nominated a candidate for
quote: an independent candidate for an office for which a candidate was nominated in the primary

claim: Independent candidates for county and state office need a declaration of intent and a petition
quote: a candidate must make a declaration of intent to run as an independent candidate

claim: A petition signature is invalid if the signer voted in the primary of a party that nominated someone for that office
quote: voted in the general or runoff primary election of a political party that made a nomination, at either primary, for the office sought by the candidate

claim: Major parties must nominate county and state candidates by primary
quote: must be nominated by primary election, held as provided by this code

claim: Plurality is the default rule for winning office
quote: to be elected to a public office, a candidate must receive more votes than any other candidate for the office

claim: Where a majority is required and nobody gets one, a runoff follows
quote: If no candidate for a particular office receives the vote necessary to be elected in an election requiring a majority vote, a runoff election for that office is required.

claim: A city with terms longer than two years must elect its whole governing body by majority vote
quote: must elect all of the members of its governing body by majority vote of the qualified voters in such municipality

claim: Any city, home rule or general law, may lengthen terms to at most four years
quote: for a longer term of office than two (2) years for its officers, either elective or appointive, or both, but not to exceed four (4) years

claim: Cities over 5,000 people may adopt a home rule charter
quote: Cities having more than five thousand (5000) inhabitants may, by a majority vote of the qualified voters of said city

claim: A home rule city keeps its charter if its population later falls to 5,000 or fewer
quote: If the number of inhabitants of cities that have adopted or amended their charters under this section is reduced to five thousand (5000) or fewer

claim: No charter may conflict with the constitution or general state law
quote: no charter or any ordinance passed under said charter shall contain any provision inconsistent with the Constitution of the State, or of the general laws enacted by the Legislature of this State

claim: A home rule city may adopt any form of government
quote: The municipality may adopt and operate under any form of government, including the aldermanic or commission form.

claim: A home rule charter may set some candidate application requirements, but not filing deadlines
quote: This section does not authorize a city charter requirement in connection with the timely filing of an application

claim: Texas municipalities are Type A, B or C general-law, home rule, or special-law
quote: A municipality is a Type C general-law municipality if it

claim: A Type A town may rename itself a city by ordinance, with no change in powers
quote: A change in designation does not affect the municipality's corporate existence or powers.

claim: Type A: mayor and five aldermen at large, or a mayor and two aldermen per ward
quote: the governing body consists of a mayor and five aldermen who are elected by the qualified voters of the municipality

claim: Type A: two-year terms by default
quote: The mayor and aldermen of the municipality are elected for a term of two years unless a longer term is established

claim: Type A: plurality wins
quote: To be elected to an office of the municipality, a person must receive more votes than any other person for the office.

claim: Type B: mayor, five aldermen and a marshal are elected
quote: the county judge of the county in which the municipality is located shall order an election for a mayor, five aldermen, and a marshal

claim: Type B: one-year terms by default, or two-year staggered terms by ordinance
quote: are elected for a term of one year unless a longer term is established

claim: Type B under 5,000 people may abolish the elected marshal
quote: The governing body of a municipality with a population of less than 5,000 by ordinance may abolish the office of marshal

claim: Type C: a mayor and two commissioners, commission form
quote: a mayor and two commissioners must be elected

claim: Type C: two-year terms by default
quote: The mayor and commissioners of the municipality serve for a term of two years unless a longer term is established

claim: Type A requires 600 or more people at incorporation
quote: contains 600 or more inhabitants

claim: Type B requires 201 to 9,999 people at incorporation
quote: contains 201 to 9,999 inhabitants

claim: Every county has a commissioners court: four commissioners from precincts plus the county judge presiding
quote: The County Commissioners so chosen, with the County Judge as presiding officer, shall compose the County Commissioners Court

claim: County commissioners serve four-year terms
quote: one County Commissioner, who shall hold his office for four years

claim: The county judge is elected countywide for four years
quote: there shall be elected in each county, by the qualified voters, a County Judge

claim: Counties elect justices of the peace and constables by precinct for four years
quote: in each such precinct there shall be elected one Justice of the Peace and one Constable, each of whom shall hold his office for four years

claim: Each county elects a sheriff for four years
quote: There shall be elected by the qualified voters of each county a Sheriff, who shall hold his office for the term of four years

claim: The constitutional county home rule section was repealed in 1969
quote: Sec. 3. (Repealed Aug. 5, 1969.)

claim: School trustees serve three- or four-year staggered terms
quote: A trustee of an independent school district serves a term of three or four years.

claim: School trustee elections must coincide with a city election in the district, the November general election, or certain other local elections
quote: An election for trustees of an independent school district shall be held on the same date as:

claim: A school board may elect some or all trustees from single-member districts
quote: may order that trustees of the district are to be elected from single-member trustee districts

claim: School trustees win by plurality unless the board requires a majority by resolution
quote: that a candidate must receive a majority of the votes cast for a position or in a trustee district, as applicable, to be elected

claim: The Legislature convenes the second Tuesday in January of odd-numbered years
quote: The legislature shall convene at the seat of government in regular session at 12 noon on the second Tuesday in January of each odd-numbered year.

claim: Regular sessions last at most 140 days
quote: No Regular Session shall be of longer duration than one hundred and forty (140) days.

claim: Laws take effect 90 days after adjournment unless two-thirds vote otherwise
quote: until ninety days after the adjournment of the session at which it was enacted

claim: The governor can convene the Legislature at other times
quote: and at other times when convened by the Governor

claim: Each county has a county court, and the county judge presides over it
quote: There shall be established in each county in this State a County Court

claim: The commissioners court exercises powers over all county business
quote: shall exercise such powers and jurisdiction over all county business
